Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Quickdraw combat presentation

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

The gunner skin now uses the original seat palette directly. The gun and hitscan beam retain their own colors instead of inheriting a whole-avatar tint. Drone and lob skins also use their owner's palette directly. The view geometry is stored as immutable meshes, preserving the original vertices and tint values without asking Polygon2D to rebuild buffers on color changes.

A decrease in sampled HP starts the original 0.25-second red skin flash. Healing alone does not start a flash. After a lethal flash, the skin uses the original dark translucent dead color; the gun and beam remain independent. New lives, initial observations, departure, resync and epoch changes seed health without flashing. An empty, unfocused chat panel stays hidden so it does not obscure the actors or landing cues. Multiple HP changes coalesced into one observation produce one pulse, as in the original's replicated HP-edge behavior.

The local player's pulse follows authority HP, while remote players follow the watched HP shown with their bodies. Predicted damage alone does not create a local hurt pulse. A pulse for an old life cannot color a newly predicted respawn. These choices preserve the intent of the original replicated-health feedback; the complete Replay world's prediction and timing still differ from the old mixed-state model.

Landing rings are an addition: the original source has splash damage and a landing receipt, but no ring renderer. A ring outlines the existing 26-pixel splash radius with a two-pixel band and fades over 0.3 seconds. Its position comes from the detached Landed occurrence, so the projectile can already be gone. Local speculative events can begin immediately; watched events follow their journal policy. Update moves an active ring without restarting it, Cancel removes it, and Confirm does not replay it. Consumed IDs remain suppressed after cancellation, expiry and same-epoch resync.

The component uses the existing bounded One_Shots ledger and 64 active ring slots. Overflow is a counted cosmetic drop, not a simulation mutation or unbounded allocation. Epoch/reset handling clears active cues and seeds history; leaving a session creates a fresh ledger so independent sessions may reuse epoch one. Normal acceptance requires zero dropped rings. Broader stress and human visual comparison remain separate work.

tests/replay_quickdraw_feedback/run.sh builds an isolated game and runs its existing UI/profile gates plus three-peer combat presentation acceptance. Pure tests cover health/life boundaries and actual journal update/cancel/reappearance behavior.
